saying: Most commenters accept trading premarket evidence for postmarket monitoring only under stated conditions: prespecified, enforceable monitoring plans with triggers and thresholds, demonstrated detection speed and coverage, reversible harm, and rollback authority. Many would bar the trade for high-consequence, autonomous, or poorly observable functions. Several question whether monitoring reliably detects novel or unreported failures at all.

disagreement.text: Most commenters would bound the trade with explicit conditions and carve-outs for high-consequence, irreversible, or autonomous functions, and some reject it outright as unsuited to a new technology; a minority urges broad latitude, with market forces as the main constraint and a rule that requirements not exceed those on existing care.

sides.summary: Allow generative AI wide latitude; regulatory requirements should not exceed the human standard of care being replaced.
Permit reduced premarket evidence only under enforceable, verified monitoring conditions, or not at all for high-consequence and autonomous functions.
